models_evaluated: Custom AI model for intracranial haemorrhage detection trained on open-access RSNA-type CT slice dataset

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ICH detection AI on local institutional historical CT scans vs reference standard
links.effect: AUC 0.842 (95% CI 0.791-0.894); at ≥50% threshold 73% sensitivity, 79% specificity, 18.6% PPV, 97.8% NPV, 78.6% accuracy on 1372 local scans (6.1% ICH).
links.quote: The model achieved an area under the curve of 0.842 (95% confidence interval=0.791-0.894; P<0.001) for scan-based detection of ICH.

links.outcome: False-negative scans before vs after manual review of model-nominated CT slices
links.effect: 22 false-negative scans reduced to six false-negative scans by manual review of the five model-nominated slices.
links.quote: There were 62 true-positive scans and 22 false-negative scans, which could be reduced to six false-negative scans by manual review of model-nominated CT slices.

screen.reason: The study validates an ICH detection algorithm on retrospective institutional data and specifically evaluates the effect of manual clinician review of model-nominated candidate slices on reducing false negatives.

primary.practice: clinician manual review of top model-nominated slices
